news.title: The Week in Numbers: CXMT debut stuns, Microsoft's market cap soars
news.summary:
STORY: From CXMT's big hitter IPO to Microsoft's largest one-day gain... This is the Week in Numbers. 

:: Week in Numbers 

:: 466%

466% was how much shares of CXMT soared by in their Shanghai trading debut...

catapulting the chipmaker to the top of China's stock market by valuation...

despite a recent sell off in global tech stocks.

Data showed the one-day surge was the largest among the world's 10 biggest IPOs this year by deal value.

And lifted CXMT's market capitalization to $487.73 billion.

CXMT has emerged as a key pillar of Beijing’s drive to build a self-sufficient chip industry.

The explosive debut crowned CXMT as China's most valuable listed company.

:: 17%

South Korea's benchmark KOSPI jumped 17% as the battered market made a record comeback....

stirring hopes that a recent rout in AI-related stocks had run out of steam.

Reversing steep losses from earlier in the week, the reversal followed surges in AI heavyweights Microsoft and Amazon...

lifting chip stocks broadly after upbeat earnings and forecasts from both.

:: $99 million

There was a  $99 million loss in the first quarter of the year for Shein as it  heads into its Hong Kong IPO.

Shein blamed slowing U.S. sales after Washington scrapped a duty exemption on small packages...

plus a one-off $328 million accounting charge.

Selina Li is Reuters Asia financial services correspondent:

"I think one thing that is for sure, we know that fast fashion isn't going away, but customers should expect those $3 items to get noticeably pricier as global trade rules catch up with the business model." 

:: 16%

16% was the second-quarter drop at British Airways owner IAG.

It's been weighed down by soaring fuel costs and weak travel demand linked to the Middle East conflict...

and said it now expects capacity to be flat this year.

IAG, which also owns Iberia and Aer Lingus, said it saw an adverse impact from higher fuel prices from March onwards...

as fuel costs and emissions charges jumped.

:: $450 billion

Microsoft added nearly $450 billion in market value.

That was the largest one-day gain on record for a company...

after it forecast stronger-than-expected cloud growth and signaled continued cash generation through its new fiscal year.

The software giant's shares closed up more than 15%, lifting its market capitalization to $3.35 trillion...

surpassing chip giant Nvidia's previous record one-day gain.

The results offered fresh evidence that Microsoft's massive AI investments are beginning to pay off.
